name: Hooding Hardstick
description: Both rods are gripped in one fist at chest height with the cord taut, forming a short guard bar before the body.

name: Doweldash
description: The free rod is lifted past the ear and dropped straight down onto the opponent's collarbone or forearm.

name: Whirrblow
description: A flat sideways swing carries the free rod across at rib height, wrist leading and elbow tucked close.

name: Forward Sidespin
description: A short upward flick of the wrist lifts the free rod's tip into the soft underside of the chin.

name: Swaying Fliparound
description: Small gliding shuffles take the user half a pace back while both hands reseat the rods for the next swing.

name: Lowered Gripstick
description: Both rods cross at the wrist and turn an incoming forearm strike aside along their slope.

name: Folded Swingstick
description: Beside the hip the free rod turns in slow wide circles, loosening the wrist and teaching the cord's path.

name: Folded Roundstick
description: The free rod traces a figure-eight before the chest, brushing aside light jabs and thrown scraps.

name: Dowelblow
description: Turning the palm outward, the user snaps the free rod backhanded across the opponent's near shoulder.

name: Straight Chainjoint
description: The free rod swings in a low arc and rakes the shin of an opponent stepping forward.

name: Rodhop
description: A quarter turn on the lead foot takes the body off the line while the rod finishes its swing.

name: Clean Octastick
description: Holding both rods close, the user drives the capped end of one rod straight into the opponent's midsection.

name: Tiedend Stay
description: After a miss the rod is hauled into the crook of the elbow, closing the opening along the user's flank.

name: Lowered Cordjoint
description: Standing square with the cord stretched across the chest, the user braces against shoves with the taut link.

name: Clackbump
description: The grip rod is driven forward by the heel of the hand so its butt end strikes the sternum.

name: Sudden Shoulderroll
description: A rolling turn of the wrist whips the far rod round to smack the side of the opponent's head.

name: Rodhusk
description: The taut cord is raised to meet an incoming stick or arm and slides it off the body's line.

name: Backward Cascade
description: A sidestep off the centerline is followed by a quick snap of the free rod against the opponent's wrist.

name: Snug Gripstick
description: One rod lies across the back of the shoulder with the other hanging, keeping the weapon guarded and half hidden.

name: Short Stickend
description: One rod is rolled across the back of the neck and released so the other lands on the opponent's side.

name: Capstick Pause
description: The returning rod is trapped in the armpit, killing its momentum and readying the next movement.

name: Staveblow
description: Passing the rod beneath the elbow into the other hand, the user swings from an unexpected side.

name: Level Roundstick
description: The free rod is caught in the off hand and dropped again at once, keeping the opponent guessing the angle.

name: Clackdash
description: A flick over the shoulder sends the free rod backward into an opponent closing from behind.

name: Quiet Neckwrap
description: The user advances with both rods held low against the thigh, shortening strides so the cord never tangles.

name: Rodcowl
description: Sliding the palm to the end of the rod lengthens reach and spoils the opponent's measured distance.

name: Solid Chainjoint
description: Weight sinks onto bent knees while the swivel hangs at the belt, the rods ready to rise.

name: Crisp Backspin
description: The free rod whips from the swivel at a slant and lands across the opponent's upper arm.

name: Snug Swingstick
description: The rod returns across the body and knocks a low kick aside with its flat side.

name: Rodbump
description: A tiny arc of the rod raps the knuckles of the opponent's leading hand, loosening their hold.

name: Turning Shoulderroll
description: The cord hooks around the opponent's wrist and pulls across, tying the arm up for a moment.

name: Clackcowl
description: Stepping back, the user keeps the swivel turning in a small ring that deflects follow-up jabs.

name: Tight Hardstick
description: A thin thread of qi runs through the held cord, stiffening the guard bar across the chest.

name: Wide Neckwrap
description: The rod strikes and, fed by a pulse of qi, springs back along the cord to the wrist.

name: Roddrop
description: The rod bounces off the target and returns for a second hit upon the same spot.

name: Easing Octastick
description: A light push of qi through the soles carries the user a pace forward as the free rod swings ahead.

name: Clackstay
description: A rod rebounding off the forearm is turned outward to knock aside a blow aimed at the ribs.

name: Whirrhit
description: Qi gathered in the capped end of the grip rod drives a short jab past the opponent's guard.

name: Locking Cordjoint
description: A sharp snap of the cord beside the opponent's hands ruffles their grip and breaks a swing's rhythm.

name: Solid Capstick
description: The free rod spins in a steady vertical ring before the body, screening against thrown stones and low jabs.

name: Planted Hardstick
description: The rod sweeps from hip to opposite shoulder, parrying an outside thrust away from the ribs.

name: Rodblow
description: Having turned a blow aside, the rod loops around and cracks against the attacker's striking arm.

name: Roundstick Wedge
description: Both rods rise overhead on a taut cord to catch and hold the fall of a cudgel stroke.

name: Clackdodge
description: A gliding backward step opens distance while the rod parries, keeping the user just beyond reach.

name: Tiedend Lid
description: The spinning rod clips the opponent's wrist mid-swing and spoils the angle of their attack.

name: Cascade Cowl
description: The hinge link slips over an attacker's forearm and the rods are pulled together, snaring the arm.

name: Towing Fliparound
description: The cord winds once around a spear or stick shaft, locking the weapon fast while the user steps in.

name: Tripping Backspin
description: Pinching the opponent's wrist between cord and rod, the user turns it outward until the grip opens.

name: Lowered Stickend
description: The two rods close like shears upon a descending stick and pin it against the user's chest.

name: Stavedrop
description: Letting go of a caught shaft, the user snaps the free rod into the opponent's exposed jaw.

name: Leaden Fliparound
description: The free rod is sent round a low circle from the hip and cuts across the opponent's thigh.

name: Low Tiedend
description: Swung up in a tall circle beside the ear, the rod comes down on the opponent's head or shoulder.

name: Clackhusk
description: As the orbit closes, the returning rod is caught across the forearm to take a stray blow.

name: Stavecowl
description: A continuous waist-high ring of the rod turns the user's whole flank into a moving fence.

name: Easing Gripstick
description: A step along the orbit's outer edge slips the user past an advancing opponent's weapon arm.

name: Fouling Sidespin
description: Pulling the rod sharply inward drags the opponent's hand with it and breaks their balance forward.

name: Straight Octastick
description: Both rods circle in opposite directions, and one is let fly at the end to hit the ribs.

name: Solid Cordjoint
description: The circling rod is stopped flat against the hip, making a firm bar against a lunge.

name: Snug Capstick
description: Qi stiffens the arms as the rods are clenched together, and the braced bar takes a shove without yielding.

name: Quick Neckwrap
description: Loosening the grip, the user lets the free rod leap outward to land on the opponent's chest.

name: Downward Sidespin
description: With fingers slack, the rod lashes out on its full cord and stings the opponent's far shoulder.

name: Rodstay
description: A sudden clench halts a swinging rod mid-arc, so the opponent misjudges the cord's remaining reach.

name: Cascade Dodge
description: Braced against the rear foot, the user drives forward half a pace with the rods held tight.

name: Square Shoulderroll
description: A backhand release sends the rod slashing across at the opponent's neck line and snapping home.

name: Resting Swingstick
description: Dropping the brace, the user lets a blow slide off the rods and resets the stance.
